topic: How a block of ice becomes a refrigerator

lines.say: This is a block of ice. It keeps your food cold.
But it melts all over your kitchen floor.
So you put it in a wooden box, lined with tin, with a tray to catch the water.
But every few days the ice is gone, and the iceman has to bring you more.
So you swap the ice for a liquid that boils at minus twenty-six degrees.
You run it through thin pipes inside the box. As it boils, it soaks up the heat from your food.
But now the pipes are full of warm gas.
So you add a compressor, that squeezes the gas until it's hotter than your kitchen.
It flows through coils on the back and dumps that heat into the room. That's why the back of your fridge is warm.
Now it's a liquid again. It squeezes through a tube thinner than spaghetti, the pressure drops, and it's freezing cold again.
But the compressor never stops, and your milk turns to ice.
So you add a thermostat, that switches it off when it's cold enough.
But cold air leaks out around the door.
So you add a rubber seal with a magnet inside.
But frost builds up on the cold pipes.
So a little heater melts it, and the water drips into a tray on the hot compressor, where it dries up.
Add some shelves, and a light that turns on when you open the door.
Congratulations. You have built a refrigerator.
